description: Automated accessibility verification (axe) across light AND dark themes, dark/light SVG legibility, and spec/README documentation. Closes Issue #22 criterion (2) 'no serious violations from an automated checker' and criterion (3) 'connectors/logos remain legible in both dark and light'. Also keeps the graded spec-driven-dev artifacts truthful (specs + both READMEs). Depends on FEAT-001 (theming + @axe-core/playwright + chromium) and FEAT-002 (keyboard nav) being complete.
steps: Add a Playwright a11y e2e (frontend/e2e/a11y.spec.ts) using @axe-core/playwright (installed in FEAT-001). For the main pages — home bracket (/season/<default>), a series detail page (a known final series id from the offline seed), and the accuracy page (/accuracy) — run an AxeBuilder scan in BOTH light and dark themes and assert there are NO violations with impact 'serious' or 'critical'. Drive the theme by setting localStorage 'mlb.theme' before load (e.g. page.addInitScript to set localStorage then reload) or by toggling the ThemeToggle UI, then confirm document.documentElement[data-theme] is the expected value before scanning. Reuse the offline-seed/route-stub patterns in frontend/e2e/fixtures.ts and the known series ids used by detail.spec.ts/accuracy.spec.ts.

Capture dark-mode screenshots in the e2e run for visual inspection of criterion (3): in a Playwright test, load the home bracket in dark theme and take a full-page screenshot (into frontend/test-results, which is gitignored) so bracket connector lines/borders and the SVG logos/marks are visibly legible. These screenshots are diagnostic (not committed snapshots).

Ensure the SVG assets (frontend/src/assets/*.svg: al, nl, ws, brand, hero, baseball) and bracket connector lines/borders remain legible on the dark background. The league marks use white strokes/fills and sit on their own colored discs so they likely survive, but verify: if any mark or the bracket border/connector relies on a near-white stroke that disappears on dark, make it theme-aware (e.g. drive the stroke/border via a CSS variable, use currentColor, or add a subtle outline/background behind marks in dark mode via styles.css). Do not alter brand identity colors unnecessarily; prefer CSS-variable-driven borders/outlines over editing the SVG fills. Confirm the badge discs + abbreviations (now using readableTextColor) read correctly in dark mode too.

Update the spec set under .kiro/specs/mlb-postseason/: add/extend requirements.md with the dark-mode + accessibility requirement (prefers-color-scheme + manual localStorage toggle 'mlb.theme'; auto AA text color on team badges; bracket keyboard navigation + SR labels; axe no serious/critical violations in light+dark), update design.md with the theming mechanism (CSS variables + data-theme + matchMedia + localStorage, the pure resolveTheme and readableTextColor helpers, the roving-tabindex keyboard model, the @axe-core/playwright e2e), and add the corresponding tasks to tasks.md. Keep the spec describing the system AS ACTUALLY BUILT (match the real module names/paths).

Update README.md with a concise, truthful section on dark mode and accessibility: the theme toggle (System/Light/Dark) persisted to localStorage 'mlb.theme' following prefers-color-scheme, automatic WCAG-AA badge text color, bracket keyboard navigation + screen-reader labels, and that an automated axe check runs in the Playwright e2e across light and dark with no serious/critical violations. Note @axe-core/playwright was added as a frontend devDependency.

Mirror the same additions in README.ja.md in natural Japanese so both READMEs stay in sync and truthful (dark mode = ダークモード, theme toggle, prefers-color-scheme 追従, localStorage 保存, バッジ文字色の自動コントラスト, ブラケットのキーボード操作とスクリーンリーダー向けラベル, axe による自動チェック).

Run the full verification suite from repo root (PATH prefix): `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run test:e2e -w @mlb/frontend` (a11y + keyboard + existing specs all green; axe reports no serious/critical in light AND dark), and `npm run synth` (cdk synth regression guard, no AWS calls). Do NOT run cdk deploy.
acceptance_criteria: frontend/e2e/a11y.spec.ts scans home, detail, and accuracy pages in BOTH light and dark with @axe-core/playwright and asserts zero 'serious'/'critical' violations; the test passes.

The e2e run captures a dark-mode home screenshot and the bracket connectors/borders and SVG league marks/logos are legible in dark mode (any that weren't are made theme-aware via CSS variables/currentColor without harming light mode).
.kiro/specs/mlb-postseason/{requirements.md,design.md,tasks.md} describe the dark mode + accessibility feature as actually built.

README.md AND README.ja.md both document dark mode (System/Light/Dark toggle, prefers-color-scheme, localStorage 'mlb.theme'), auto AA badge text color, bracket keyboard nav + SR labels, and the axe e2e check — consistently in English and Japanese.
`npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run test:e2e -w @mlb/frontend`, and `npm run synth` all pass; no serious/critical axe violations in either theme.
verification: PATH="/root/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH" npm run test:e2e -w @mlb/frontend  (a11y.spec.ts: no serious/critical violations in light AND dark; keyboard + existing specs green)
PATH="/root/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH" npm run synth  (cdk synth succeeds, no AWS calls)
findings:
DONE. Commits: f2b0dec (feat: axe e2e + dark contrast fix), 89b01fa (docs: specs + both READMEs).

WHAT I DID:
1. Added frontend/e2e/a11y.spec.ts using @axe-core/playwright (AxeBuilder scoped to wcag2a/2aa/21a/21aa). Scans home bracket (2024 results-only, offline seed), a FINAL series detail page (2026 stubbed via stubBracket2026, id 2026-al-championship-117-136 from fixtures.ts), and /accuracy in BOTH light and dark; asserts zero serious/critical violations. Theme driven deterministically by seeding localStorage 'mlb.theme' to literal 'light'/'dark' via page.addInitScript BEFORE load, then asserting html[data-theme] before scanning. A separate diagnostic test captures a full-page dark home screenshot to test-results/home-dark.png (gitignored).
2. CONTRAST FIX (CSS-only, styles.css): the axe scan surfaced serious color-contrast violations ONLY in dark mode on elements using color: var(--navy) as foreground text on dark surfaces (.bracket__round-title, .prediction__title, .standings__title, .detail__title/.detail__games-title/.detail__game-num/.series-card__game-num, .detail__back). Root cause: --navy is used BOTH as a fill (header gradient, buttons, selected states) and as foreground text. Introduced a dedicated --heading variable (light #1b3a6b == --navy; dark #8fb4f2, >=5.9:1 on every dark surface) and repointed all `color: var(--navy)` -> `color: var(--heading)`. Navy fills/gradients unchanged, light mode visually unchanged. No SVG edits needed: al/nl/ws/brand/hero/baseball all sit on self-colored discs/gradients and stay legible on dark (verified via screenshot + axe).
3. Updated .kiro/specs/mlb-postseason/: added Requirement 15 (dark mode + a11y), a 'Dark mode and accessibility (Issue #22)' design section (theme.ts pure core, ThemeContext.tsx, ThemeToggle.tsx, readableTextColor.ts, roving-tabindex BracketView, --heading contrast fix, @axe-core/playwright e2e), and task section A1-A3 in tasks.md. Described AS BUILT (real module names).
4. Updated README.md AND README.ja.md: Overview bullet + a 'Dark mode and accessibility' section (System/Light/Dark toggle, prefers-color-scheme, localStorage 'mlb.theme', auto AA badge text color, roving-tabindex keyboard nav + SR labels, axe e2e across light+dark no serious/critical, @axe-core/playwright devDependency).

VERIFICATION (all PATH-prefixed from repo root):
- npm run build: PASS.
- npm run test:e2e -w @mlb/frontend: PASS (34/34; new a11y.spec.ts: 7/7, zero serious/critical in light AND dark; keyboard + all existing specs green).
- npm run synth: PASS (no AWS calls).
- npm test (unit): frontend 85/85, backend 92/92, infra 8/8 PASS. shared 33/34 with ONE flaky failure in shared/src/integrity.property.test.ts (NOT mine, NOT Issue #22 scope). PRE-EXISTING FLAKE: verified by git stash (passed with my docs stashed under a different random seed) and 3x deterministic reruns (34/34 each). Root cause is in the TEST's fast-check arbitrary, which can generate two series sharing the same id; the assertion `series.find(s => s.id === warning.seriesId)` then resolves to the WRONG (first) duplicate, so an expect(...).toBeDefined() can fail for rare seeds. My changes are CSS + docs only and cannot affect a shared TS property test. Left untouched to avoid scope-creep into an unrelated workspace; flagged here for the integrity-check (#13) owner. If CI pins a bad seed, re-run or dedupe series ids in bracketArb().

NOTE: did NOT push / open PR / deploy (per constraints).
